hook: Borrowman spent more than a decade inside Colgate-Palmolive's Hill's Pet Nutrition division building global digital marketing systems before moving to the European digital transformation role and then into enterprise AI. Her Davos 2026 appearance placed her in the small cohort of marketing leaders publicly shaping the governance and brand questions that agentic AI raises, specifically, how leadership principles should be embedded directly into AI architecture rather than applied after the fact.
name: Christy Borrowman

quote.text: As AI systems move from generating outputs to executing decisions, leadership principles should be embedded directly into AI architecture.

reading.body:
Christy Borrowman's career argues that enterprise AI governance is most credibly shaped by people who built the underlying digital systems it is replacing, not by those who arrived at the governance question from the outside.

Her path runs from agency work through a global marketing director role inside Hill's Pet Nutrition, a division the data values at USD 2.3 billion, then through direct-to-consumer operations and contact center transformation, then into European digital transformation, and now into enterprise-wide agentic commerce. Each step added operational depth before the next raised the level of abstraction. That sequence matters because agentic AI, systems that execute decisions rather than generate suggestions, creates accountability questions that are hard to answer without knowing how the underlying workflows actually function.

The Davos 2026 appearance and the quote attributed to it point to a specific governance position: leadership principles should be embedded into AI architecture rather than applied afterward. The data does not explain how that embedding works in practice, and it offers no independent assessment of the outcomes at Colgate-Palmolive. What it does establish is the professional trajectory and the public forum in which the position was stated. The Microsoft advisory role and the PEX board membership are listed without detail, so they mark professional affiliations rather than illuminate specific contributions.
